resale_co.name: Certificate of Continued Occupancy
resale_co.lead_time: Applications can be turned in any time with the fee; call during office hours to schedule the first inspection. Inspections are on Wednesday evenings.
requirements: Water test meeting NJDEP and federal EPA chemical, bacteriological and gross alpha limits (not needed on public water)
Septic certification (not needed on public sewer)
Chimney certification for all fossil fuel systems
Fire extinguisher (Township packet includes the 2005 state extinguisher memo)
Electrical panel box labeled; 100 amp service
Corrections and re-inspections must be done before occupancy

fees.label: Certificate of Continued Occupancy, initial inspection

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill in the Quinton Township Certificate of Continued Occupancy Application (Department of Housing, PO Box 65, Quinton, NJ 08072) and turn it in with the fee (the form records payment by check). Then call the Housing Office during office hours (Wednesdays 4 pm to 5:30 pm) to schedule the first inspection; inspections are held Wednesday evenings. Have the water test, septic certification and chimney certification ready before the certificate can be issued.

resale_co.notes: The Township Housing Office posts a Certificate of Continued Occupancy application that names an owner/seller and a buyer/tenant, with a $40.00 initial inspection fee and a $40.00 re-inspection fee, and a guideline listing what must be provided before the certificate is issued. The fee amounts are printed on an undated scanned form and were read visually. A web search summary of Township Code Chapter 150, Housing (ecode360, not opened and not quoted here) described a certificate of occupancy being required on a change of owner or tenant and not issued unless taxes, sewer charges and other municipal assessments are current; that wording is a lead only. The Housing Office page also says the certificate of occupancy fee for rental units built before 1979 will be $60 and a Certificate of Re-occupancy fee is $80 (including $20 for the NJ Lead Hazard Control Fund); those relate to the rental lead-safe program, not to a 1-2 family sale. The application form header prints 856-935-7482; the current Housing Office page lists Robert Schmid at 856-935-2325 Ext. 5 and the office line 856-935-0272. The email zoning@quintonnj.com is from the mailto link on the Housing Office page.

requirements: Township CCO guideline requires smoke detectors, carbon monoxide alarms and a fire extinguisher before the certificate is issued; the extinguisher sheet in the Township packet is a 2005 state memo (2A:10B:C, no more than 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, top no more than 5 feet above the floor)

authorities.name: Not confirmed. Likely the Quinton Township Housing Office, which checks smoke detectors, CO alarms and the fire extinguisher for the Certificate of Continued Occupancy
authorities.how_to_apply: No separate smoke/CO certificate application or fee is published. The Township Certificate of Continued Occupancy guideline requires smoke detectors, CO alarms and a fire extinguisher before the certificate is issued. The NJ DCA online smoke certificate application does not offer Quinton (the DCA marks it smoke-certificate exempt), so ask the Housing Office who issues the smoke/CO certificate for a sale.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety is Quinton's fire code enforcing agency (LEA registry code S), and the state fire directory (listed there as Quinton Township 1711) names "NJ Division Fire Safety" for smoke detector compliance. But the DCA does not issue smoke certificates for Quinton through its online route: the DCA's July 17, 2026 state towns list shows Quinton without the "SC" (smoke certs) flag, and the fire district feed used by the DCA online smoke application marks QUINTON TWP-001 as smoke-certificate exempt, which the application uses to leave it out of the list of districts a private home can choose. The Township's own Certificate of Continued Occupancy requires smoke detectors, CO alarms and a fire extinguisher, so the Housing Office inspection most likely covers the smoke/CO check, but no official page says who issues the certificate or what it costs. The Township's Fire Safety Memorandum is a 2005 DCA memo on extinguishers; the state removed the extinguisher from the state requirement by P.L.2025, c.19, but the Township guideline still lists it.

other_items.label: Water test
other_items.detail: Water test meeting NJDEP and federal EPA chemical, bacteriological and gross alpha limits, unless on a public water system.

other_items.label: Septic certification
other_items.detail: Septic certification unless on public sewer; the Township posts a septic certification guideline and a list of Salem County Department of Health recognized septic inspectors.

other_items.label: Chimney certification
other_items.detail: Chimney certification for all fossil fuel systems.
